title: Unified Inference Product Hub: Overview, PRDs, Roadmap & Pricing (Mar 2028)
author: Asha Patel
content:
## Summary

This document consolidates the Unified Inference product portfolio: product overview, PRD and requirements, high-level design specs, roadmap and themes through H2 2028, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes for the current launch. It is intended as the canonical product hub for engineering, sales, and customer-facing teams.

---

## 1. Product overview

Redwood Unified Inference is a single product surface that provides consistent, cost-aware LLM inference across Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. Primary capabilities: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output.

Key value props:
- Production-grade latency and throughput with built-in fallbacks and routing policies.
- Predictable economics via Dedicated capacity and cost controls (batching, caching, quantization).
- Unified developer experience (same API, SDKs, and rollout controls across deployment modes).

Target customers: AI-native startups, mid-market and enterprise product teams, and internal platform teams.

---

## 2. Goals & success metrics (90 days / 6 months)

Primary objectives:
- Increase self-serve adoption of Dedicated and Private by 35% in Q2 2028.
- Reduce token cost per 1k tokens by 18% via Optimize recommendations and improved batching.
- Achieve API p50 latency <= 60ms for typical chat workloads on hosted SLO model.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- MRR from Dedicated commitments (target +22% QoQ).
- Platform availability (SLA alignment): 99.95% monthly uptime for Dedicated.
- Regression rate on quality monitoring < 1% post-release.
- Number of customers using rollout controls (canary/A-B) > 25.

---

## 3. PRD & requirements

Scope: Core Unified Inference features for the next release (v2028.03): model routing policies, cost-aware fallback behaviors, upgraded batching controls, and pricing packaging for Dedicated.

Must-have user stories:
1. As an engineer, I want a per-route model routing policy so I can prioritize latency or cost per endpoint.
2. As a platform admin, I want automatic fallback to a quantized model variant when capacity is constrained.
3. As a product manager, I want rollout controls (canary, percentage rollouts) integrated with tracing and rollback.
4. As a procurement lead, I want clear Dedicated pricing bands and an ROI worksheet to justify a 3-12 month commitment.

Non-functional requirements:
- Security: All customer inference logs must be encrypted at rest and support KMS integration.
- Scalability: System should handle 10x peak Q1 traffic with autoscaling policies in Dedicated.
- Observability: Per-route token costs, p50/p95 latency, error rates, and KV cache hit ratios available in Console.
- Backwards compatibility: API surface must accept existing client SDKs with opt-in for new routing fields.

Constraints and dependencies:
- GPU kernel improvements (eng-serving-runtime) for quantized variants (dependency ENG-SR-237).
- Billing integration and metering accuracy (finance-and-legal).
- Console UX changes (eng-developer-experience) for rollout controls and pricing calculators.

Acceptance criteria:
- E2E tests demonstrating fallback flows under synthetic capacity saturation.
- Pricing page updated and validated by finance/legal and sales.
- Migration guide published for customers moving from legacy endpoints.

---

## 4. Design specs (high level)

Architecture overview:
- Control plane: request routing, policy evaluation, rollout management, and telemetry ingestion.
- Serving plane: model variants (full FP16, Q4/Q8 quantized), batching layer, KV cache, and kernel selection libraries.
- Storage & billing: metering pipeline for token counting, cost attribution, and invoice exports.

APIs and payloads:
- /v1/routes (POST/GET/PUT): route config with fields: model_preference[], fallback_policy, routing_strategy (latency|cost|region), rollout (canary_percent, rollout_schedule).
- /v1/infer (existing): accepts new header X-Redwood-Route to evaluate route policy server-side.

Policy evaluation sequence (runtime):
1. Evaluate explicit route config.
2. Check cached capacity hints and select model variant.
3. Apply batching window based on route latency SLO.
4. Emit telemetry and cost attribution event.

Operational knobs (exposed in Console):
- Batching window (ms), max batch size, KV cache TTL, quantization profile (recommended per model), fallback threshold (capacity %).

Security & compliance notes:
- All control plane actions are recorded with actor IDs and stored for 365 days.
- Private deployments require an on-prem control plane option and integration guide.

---

## 5. Roadmap & themes (H2 2028 focus)

Themes:
- Reliability & graceful degradation: expand fallback catalog and multi-region routing.
- Cost control & forecasting: improved Optimize recommendations and commitment tooling.
- Enterprise readiness: enhanced RBAC, longer audit retention, and private on-prem upgrades.

Quarterly milestones:
- Q2 2028: Launch v2028.03 (routing policies, fallback, pricing bands for Dedicated).
- Q3 2028: Autoscaling policy improvements, rollout analytics, and dedicated ROI calculator in Console.
- Q4 2028: Private on-prem installer v2 with HSM/KMS examples and extended audit retention.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Kernel/quantization regressions causing quality drops. Mitigation: gated rollout with automatic rollback on quality monitors.
- Risk: Billing mismatch during Dedicated transitions. Mitigation: shadow billing pipeline and reconciliation jobs prior to customer billing.

---

## 6. Pricing & packaging notes

Pricing tiers (summary):
- Free / Dev: Hosted API sandbox, limited rate and 30k tokens/day.
- Pay-as-you-go (Hosted): standard per-token pricing with volume discounts at thresholds 1M, 10M, 100M tokens.
- Dedicated: monthly committed GPU pools with tiered discounts (3-month, 12-month). Pricing bands depend on committed concurrency and model family (Llama-class vs larger foundation models).
- Private: license + support fee, with optional on-prem packaging and installation services.

Dedicated packaging guidance (sales playbook excerpt):
- Small (S): 4-8 GPU pool, entry throughput, 10% discount, 3 month min.
- Medium (M): 16-32 GPU pool, production throughput, 20% discount, 6 month min.
- Large (L): 64+ GPU pool, SLA backed, 30% discount, 12 month min + enterprise support.

Add-ons and usage controls:
- Optimize Premium: model recommendation engine, extended retention for evals, per-route cost simulation.
- SLA Upgrades: 99.95% to 99.99% availability with on-call rotation.

Billing & metering notes:
- Tokens are measured at the control plane using normalized tokenization (BPE) to avoid model tokenizer variance.
- Dedicated invoices include baseline committed spend and overage at a pre-negotiated per-token rate.

---

## 7. Release notes (v2028.03)

Highlights:
- Introduced per-route routing policies and cost-aware fallback behavior.
- Console: rollout controls (canary percent, staged rollouts) and per-route cost dashboards.
- New pricing bands and Dedicated packaging published.

Important migration notes:
1. Update client SDKs to v3.2 to include route header support and new rollout APIs.
2. Customers using legacy Dedicated endpoints must rebind routes to the Unified API by 2028-06-01.
3. If you rely on model tokenizer counts for billing reconciliation, switch to control plane metering before next billing cycle.

Known issues (v2028.03):
- Quantized variant may show minor generation variance for rare tokens in LLM-X family (ENG-SR-1412). Temporary mitigation: toggle fallback_policy to prefer FP16 for routes with strict quality requirements.
